manifest.name: dsh-session-query-vector
manifest.description: Semantic session search backend for DSH, backed by Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint
manifest.author: haomin li

bundle.text:
# dsh-session-query-vector bundle patch.
#
# A bundle patch is a layer over the profile tree: rows are addressed by id and
# the last write wins. Two things happen here:
#
#   1. The official SQLite backend is switched off. Both it and this package
#      extend the same `sessionQuery` service, so exactly one backend may be
#      mounted. Delete this row if you disable this bundle instead.
#   2. This package's backend is inserted, with defaults that point at a local
#      Ollama. Point `baseUrl`/`apiKey`/`embedModel` at whatever you index with —
#      the query side and indexer.mjs must embed with the SAME model, or the
#      stored vectors and the query vector live in different spaces.
- id: session-query-sqlite
  disabled: true

- insert:
    - id: session-query-vector
      name: 'dsh-session-query-vector'
      config:
        provider: ollama
        baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:11434'
        embedModel: bge-m3
        openAt: first-search

readme.text:
A semantic session-search backend for DSH, backed by Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint.

DSH ships a SQLite full-text backend (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query-sqlite`) that answers "which session contained this word". This package replaces it with a vector backend that answers "which session was about this" — you ask in your own words, the query is embedded, and the closest chunks come back with their session and snippet.
It is a drop-in replacement for the official backend: both extend the same `sessionQuery` service, so exactly one of them may be mounted at a time.

| | |
|---|---|
| DSH | `0.2.1-rc.2` (developed and tested against it) |
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `~4.0.5` |
| `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` | `3.18.5` (ships with DSH) |
| Node.js | 22+ — the indexer uses the built-in `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync`) |
| An embedding endpoint | Ollama locally, or any OpenAI-compatible API |

Earlier DSH releases are untested.

| Piece | What it is |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | The **query** side — a `SessionQueryEngine` subclass mounted as a plugin. Answers searches by reading the index. Never embeds. |
| `indexer.mjs` | The **index** side — a standalone script. Walks `~/.dsh/sessions`, embeds the message text, writes the vectors. |

They are deliberately separate: search must stay fast, and embedding is slow. The query side never triggers an embedding on the search path; if the index is empty it returns nothing.
**The two sides must use the same embedding model.** Otherwise the stored vectors and the query vector live in different spaces and every score is noise. Configure `embedModel` identically in both.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add github:minhaoli/dsh-session-query-vector
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends it to `dsh.profile.bundles` and the loader mounts it on the next start.

**The bundle patch also disables the official backend**, because both register `sessionQuery`:

```yaml

- id: session-query-sqlite
  disabled: true

- insert:
    - id: session-query-vector
      name: 'dsh-session-query-vector'
      config:
        provider: ollama
        baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:11434'
        embedModel: bge-m3
        openAt: first-search
```

If you would rather keep the official backend, remove that first row and do not mount this package — they cannot coexist.

Set these in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config` rather than merging into it, so restate every key you want to keep.

```yaml

- insert:
    - id: session-query-vector
      name: 'dsh-session-query-vector'
      config:
        path: 'C:/Users/<you>/.dsh/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite'
        provider: openai
        baseUrl: 'https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1'
        apiKey: 'sk-...'
        embedModel: 'BAAI/bge-m3'
        openAt: first-search
        topK: 20
        minScore: 0.45
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `~/.dsh/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite` | Index database. Created on first use. |
| `openAt` | `first-search` | `startup` opens the DB at mount; `first-search` on the first query; `never` disables search entirely. |
| `provider` | `ollama` | `ollama` or `openai`. `openai` means any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings`. |
| `baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | Embedding endpoint. A trailing `/v1` is stripped and re-added, so `https://host/v1` and `https://host` both work. |
| `apiKey` | `""` | Sent as `Authorization: Bearer` when non-empty. Not needed for Ollama. |
| `embedModel` | `bge-m3` | Must match the indexer. |
| `embedTimeoutMs` | `120000` | Per-request timeout. |
| `topK` | `20` | Candidates pulled from the index before ranking. |
| `minScore` | `0.45` | Cosine floor. |
| `relMargin` | `0.10` | Relative cutoff: a hit is kept only if its score is within `relMargin` of the best hit. |
| `snippetChars` | `240` | Snippet length in the result. |
| `readWindowMax` | `50` | Read window for the engine's live-preferred reads. |

```http
POST {baseUrl}/api/embeddings
content-type: application/json

{ "model": "bge-m3", "prompt": "the text to embed" }

Response: `{ "embedding": [0.013, -0.021, ...] }`.

Pull the model first:

```bash
ollama pull bge-m3
```

```http
POST {baseUrl}/v1/embeddings
authorization: Bearer <apiKey>
content-type: application/json

Response: `{ "data": [{ "index": 0, "embedding": [...] }, ...] }`. Results are sorted by `data[].index` before use — some providers return them out of order.

A trailing `/v1` on `baseUrl` is stripped before `/v1/embeddings` is appended, so `https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1` does not become `/v1/v1/embeddings`.

Any endpoint that satisfies this contract works: SiliconFlow, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Together, a local vLLM or LM Studio server, and so on. Set `baseUrl`, `apiKey` and `embedModel` to whatever that provider names the model.

`indexer.mjs` is not run by DSH — start it yourself, after the query side is configured. It must be able to `import` the `@deepseek-ai/*` packages, so run it with the DSH runtime (see below).

```bash

readme.section: layered: layer 1 (user messages) first, then layer 2 (assistant messages)
readme.text:
node indexer.mjs --layer=1        # only user messages — fastest path to a usable search
node indexer.mjs --layer=2        # only assistant messages
node indexer.mjs --limit=200      # cap sessions this run
node indexer.mjs --status         # print progress, index nothing
node indexer.mjs --force          # re-index unchanged sessions
node indexer.mjs --quiet          # no progress lines, only key events
node indexer.mjs --skip-active=5  # skip sessions written in the last 5 minutes
```

readme.section: layered: layer 1 (user messages) first, then layer 2 (assistant messages)
readme.text:
| Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_HOME` | `~/.dsh` | DSH home. Everything else derives from it. |
| `DSH_MODULES` | `$DSH_HOME/node_modules/@deepseek-ai` | Where to resolve `@deepseek-ai/*`. Override for the packaged desktop app. |
| `VEC_DB` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite` | Index path — must equal the plugin's `path`. |
| `VEC_SESSIONS` | `$DSH_HOME/sessions` | Session log root. |
| `VEC_PROVIDER` | `ollama` | `ollama` or `openai` — must equal the plugin's `provider`. |
| `VEC_BASE_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | Must equal the plugin's `baseUrl`. |
| `VEC_API_KEY` | `""` | Must equal the plugin's `apiKey`. |
| `VEC_MODEL` | `bge-m3` | Must equal the plugin's `embedModel`. |
| `VEC_CHUNK` | `1200` | Characters per chunk. |
| `VEC_BATCH` | `16` | Chunks per embedding request. |
| `VEC_SUBAGENTS` | — | Set to `1` to include subagent sessions. |

readme.section: Running the indexer against the packaged desktop app
readme.text:
The Electron app's `@deepseek-ai/*` modules live inside `app.asar`, which plain `node` cannot read. Point `DSH_MODULES` at the asar and run the indexer under the app's own binary in Node mode:

```powershell
$env:ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE = '1'
$env:DSH_MODULES = 'D:/APP/deepseek harness/resources/app.asar/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/'
& 'D:\APP\deepseek harness\DeepSeek Harness.exe' indexer.mjs --status
```

readme.section: Running the indexer against the packaged desktop app
readme.text: From a source checkout, plain `node indexer.mjs` works — `DSH_MODULES` already points at real files.
One SQLite file, `application_id = 1146308690` (distinct from the official backend's), `user_version = 1`. A file whose `application_id` belongs to something else is refused rather than clobbered.

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `vec_chunks(session_id, seq, type, time, chunk_idx, text, dim, vector BLOB)` | One row per embedded chunk. Primary key `(session_id, seq, chunk_idx)`. |
| `vec_sessions(id, revision, indexed_at, chunks, cwd, layer)` | Per-session bookkeeping; `revision` drives the incremental skip. |
| `vec_queries(text, vector, dim, at)` | Query-vector cache, so repeating a search skips the embedding round trip. |
All tables are `STRICT`. Each session is one transaction, so an interrupted run never leaves a half-written session.

- **Empty results, no error.** The index has not been built, or was built with a different model. Check `--status`.
- **`database ... belongs to another application`.** `path` points at a file this package did not create.
- **`database ... is not an empty or recognized index`.** The file exists with tables but no `application_id` — point `path` somewhere else or delete it.
- **`/v1/v1/embeddings` 404.** You set `baseUrl` with a trailing `/v1` and the code already handles it; a 404 here means the provider's path differs from the OpenAI contract.
- **Both backends mounted.** `sessionQuery` is registered twice and the second mount fails. Disable `session-query-sqlite`.
